Accordingly, the appellants had been found guilty and convicted for the offence punishable -6- Cr. Therefore, submission has been made that since there is absence of ingredient of penal provision of offence under Section 364A IPC, hence the conviction made under Section 364A IPC will be said to be improper and unjustified and the judgment of conviction will be said to be not sustainable in the eye of law. -8- Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1278 of 2016 & Ors V. VII. Learned counsel for the appellants has relied upon following judgments: (i) Vishwanath Gupta v. State of Uttaranchal, (2007) 11 SCC 633 (ii) State of U.P. v. Wasif Haider, (2019) 2 SCC 303. Argument on behalf of appellant in Cr. Appeal (DB) No.867 of 2016: 14. The appellant has been convicted on the basis of allegation that appellant-Pappu Paswan was driving the alleged Bolero vehicle bearing registration no. JH-10B/1459, but none of the witnesses have deposed that the appellant-Pappu Paswan was driving the vehicle at the time when the crime was committed by the co-accused, namely, Anil Pal and Pintu Soni; and merely on the basis of confessional statement (Ext.8) of co- accused, he has been convicted in this case. II. P.W. 4-Surjit Kumar and P.W. 5, who are victims, have identified the Anil Pal Son Of Ram Pyare Pal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175905521/ 5 accused Pappu Paswan by face for the first-time during trial on the date of his examination and even P.W. 3 failed to identify the appellant during trial in dock also, therefore, identification by P.W. 4 and P.W. 5 of the appellant-Pappu Paswan for the first time in the Court ought not to have been relied upon since the - 10 - Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1278 of 2016 & Ors possibility of the accused having been shown to these witnesses either in the jail custody or during the period of transit from jail to the Court before their examination cannot be ruled out. IV. The complicity of the appellant has also been considered by the learned trial Court on the basis of recovery of mobile and the CDR containing the call details report but merely on the basis of aforesaid details of call record there cannot be any conviction unless the procedure under Section 65B of the Evidence Act will be taken recourse of. V. Mr. A.K. Sahani, learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon the judgment on the issue of TIP and the basis of conviction based upon the identification of the accused persons in the Court by making reference of the judgment rendered by Honble Apex Court in the case of Amrik Singh v. State of Punjab, (2022) 9 SCC 402 and Ramesh v. State of Karnataka, (2009) 15 SCC 35.
